target.name: Walden Robotics
target.founder: Russ Tedrake (co-founder & CEO; MIT professor, ex-SVP Large Behavior Models at Toyota Research Institute); other co-founders not publicly named

methods.name: Stage-Progression
methods.rationale: Applies typical Seed → next-stage step-up multiplier (2.5x) to $1.1B last post money.

methods.name: Peer-Median
methods.rationale: Median across 10 same-sector + similar-valuation-tier peers in Robotics & Manufacturing. Range: $1.0B - $2.3B.

data.narrative:
Walden Robotics is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company valued at $1.1B post-money following $300M in total capital raised. The valuation is assessed against a peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable, all operating in the robotics and manufacturing sector. Key private peers include Divergent ($2.3B, Series E), Exotec ($2.0B, Series D), Locus Robotics ($2.0B, Series F), Generalist AI ($2.0B, Series B), and Bedrock Robotics ($1.8B, Series B).

Two valuation methods were applied. The Stage-Progression approach applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier typical of Seed-to-next-stage advancement, yielding $2.8B. The Peer-Median method benchmarks against 10 same-sector comparables with similar valuation tier, establishing a median of $1.7B across a range of $1.0B to $2.3B. These methods triangulate to a low of $1.4B, median of $2.2B, and high of $3.2B.

The median implied valuation of $2.2B represents a 100% step-up from the current $1.1B post-money, consistent with typical Seed progression dynamics. Key uncertainties include the founder's prior role at Toyota Research Institute and the specific technical differentiation of the platform, which remain material to stage-appropriate risk adjustment. The $1.4B–$3.2B range reflects methodological divergence between peer positioning and stage-based progression mechanics.
